newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar oil output continues on upward path.
newsitem.headline: Qatar oil output continues on upward path.

text.p: Rising oil output in OPEC-member Qatar has beaten its own expectations, but the Gulf Arab state remains committed to its OPEC quota, government and industry sources said on Thursday.
The small Gulf state produced more than 650,000 barrels per day (bpd) in June and capacity is expected to rise to more than 730,000 bpd by the middle of 1998, they said.
"This only represents the state's production capacity, and not the rise in actual production itself," said an official at the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC).
"June output was simply meant to test our new production capacity and sustainability...The average output over the six month period will not be 650,000 bpd," he told Reuters.
"We are a member of OPEC and are committed to our quota of 378,000 bpd," he added.

Industry observers estimate that Qatar, along with Venezuela and Nigeria, is one of the biggest violators of OPEC quotas, pushing the 11-member group's output to 26.3 million bpd in June versus its agreed ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
Qatar's veteran energy and industry minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah is currently OPEC president.

"It is embarrassing to hear that the president's own country is producing in excess of the quota, but people don't understand that this is a temporary phase and the average won't exceed the quota much," said a QGPC official.
Industry officials said Qatar had planned to lift its combined oil and condensate production to 610,000 bpd by the end of 1997.
"But the actual output has far surpassed the target and it is now in excess of 755,000 bpd, with around 100,000 bpd of condensates coming from the North Field," said one official.
Doha has opened its foreign oil and gas fields to foreign investment in a move to lift oil capacity to one million bpd by 2000 from 400,000 bpd in the early 1990s.
Production from QGPC's Dukhan field has reached 275,000 bpd in June with an additional 135,000 bpd from the combined Bul Hanine and Maydan Mahzam fields.

Occidental Petroleum Corp's Idd El Shargi concession pumped 95,000 bpd, Atlantic Richfield Co's Al Rayyan field 34,000 bpd, Danish A.P. Moeller unit Maersk Oil's Al Shaheen 100,000 bpd and Elf Aquitaine's Al Khaleej field 17,000 bpd.
Occidental plan to lift output to an achieve an average of 100,000-105,000 bpd by early next year.
